'''Sir Martyn Poliakoff''' (born 16 December 1947)<ref name="A & C Black" /> is a British chemist known for his work on [[green chemistry]] and for being the main presenter on the popular [[YouTube]] channel ''[[Periodic Videos]]''.<ref>{{YouTube|6yT8kvHlgeg|Martyn Poliakoff talks about the Periodic Table of Videos}}</ref> The core subjects of his academic work are [[supercritical fluid]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Parrott |first1=A.J. |last2=Bourne |first2=R.A. |last3=Akien |first3=G.R. |last4=Irvine |first4=D.J. |last5=Poliakoff |first5=M. |year=2011 |title=Self-Optimizing Continuous Reactions in Supercritical Carbon Dioxide |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=50 |issue=16 |pages=3788–92 |doi=10.1002/anie.201100412 |pmid=21442710}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bourne |first1=R.A. |last2=Han |first2=X. |last3=Chapman |first3=A.O. |last4=Arrowsmith |first4=N.J. |last5=Kawanami |first5=H. |last6=Poliakoff |first6=M. |last7=George |first7=M.W. |year=2008 |title=Homogeneous photochemical oxidation via singlet O2 in supercritical CO2 |journal=Chemical Communications |issue=37 |pages=4457–59 |doi=10.1039/b806063k |pmid=18802589}}</ref> [[infrared spectroscopy]] and [[lasers]]. He is a research professor in chemistry at the [[University of Nottingham]].<ref name="Nottingham.ac.uk">{{cite web |title=Introduction to Supercritical Fluids |url=http://www.nottingham.ac.uk/supercritical/beta/mp-entry.html |access-date=5 December 2016 |website=Nottingham.ac.uk |archive-date=17 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150817095736/http://www.nottingham.ac.uk/supercritical/beta/mp-entry.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> As well as carrying out research at the University of Nottingham, he is a lecturer, teaching a number of modules including [[green chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Poliakoff |first1=M. |last2=Licence |first2=P. |year=2007 |title=Sustainable technology: Green chemistry |journal=Nature |volume=450 |issue=7171 |pages=810–12 |bibcode=2007Natur.450..810P |doi=10.1038/450810a |pmid=18064000 |s2cid=12340643}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Asfaw |first1=N. |last2=Chebude |first2=Y. |last3=Ejigu |first3=A. |last4=Hurisso |first4=B.B. |last5=Licence |first5=P. |last6=Smith |first6=R.L. |last7=Tang |first7=S.L.Y. |last8=Poliakoff |first8=M. |year=2011 |title=The 13 Principles of Green Chemistry and Engineering for a Greener Africa |journal=Green Chemistry |volume=13 |issue=5 |page=1059 |doi=10.1039/c0gc00936a}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tuck |first1=C.O. |last2=Pérez |first2=E. |last3=Horváth |first3=I.T. |author-link3=István T. Horváth |last4=Sheldon |first4=R.A. |author-link4=Roger A. Sheldon |last5=Poliakoff |first5=M. |year=2012 |title=Valorization of biomass: Deriving more value from waste |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |location=New York |volume=337 |issue=6095 |pages=695–99 |bibcode=2012Sci...337..695T |doi=10.1126/science.1218930 |pmid=22879509 |s2cid=715234}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Poliakoff was born to a [[British Jewish|British-Jewish]] mother, Ina ({{nee|Montagu}}), and a [[Russian-Jewish]] father, [[Alexander Poliakoff]]. He has a younger brother, the screenwriter and director [[Stephen Poliakoff]]. His paternal grandfather, [[Joseph Poliakoff]], was a prolific inventor of electrical devices who experienced the communist revolution in Russia first-hand, and immigrated to the United Kingdom in 1924.<ref>{{cite news |last=Poliakoff |first=Stephen |date=28 May 2008 |title=Ringside at the revolution |url=https://www.theguardian.com/stage/2008/may/28/theatre.culture |newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref>

Poliakoff was educated at [[Westminster School]].<ref name="A & C Black" /> He then studied chemistry at [[King's College, Cambridge]], graduating with a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] degree in 1969. While an undergraduate, he became close friends with [[Tony Judt]], who later became a historian and writer.<ref>{{cite web |date=11 August 2010 |title=Toast to Tony – Periodic Table of Videos |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3rhBHwQEWpQ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211214/3rhBHwQEWpQ |archive-date=14 December 2021 |access-date=5 December 2016 |publisher=YouTube}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Periodic Videos |date=7 July 2008 |title=Ruthenium (version 1) – Periodic Table of Videos |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NSi6Wosajys |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211214/NSi6Wosajys |archive-date=14 December 2021 |access-date=5 December 2016 |publisher=YouTube}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Poliakoff received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in chemistry from Cambridge in 1973 for research supervised by J.J. Turner.<ref name="Nottingham.ac.uk" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Poliakoff |first1=M. |last2=Turner |first2=J.J. |year=1970 |title=The infrared spectra of trimetal carbonyl species in frozen gas matrices at 20K |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society D: Chemical Communications |issue=16 |page=1008 |doi=10.1039/C29700001008}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |degree=DPhil |first=Martyn |last=Poliakoff |title=The matrix isolation of large molecules. The photochemistry of transition metal carbonyls |publisher=University of Cambridge |date=1973 |url=http://ulmss-newton.lib.cam.ac.uk/vwebv/holdingsInfo?bibId=12660 |oclc=500541617}}</ref>

==Career and research==
In 1972, Poliakoff moved to [[Newcastle University]] and in 1979 was appointed a lecturer at the [[University of Nottingham]],<ref name="Nottingham.ac.uk" /> where he was subsequently promoted to professor in 1991.<ref name="A & C Black" /> His research has been funded by the [[EPSRC]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Grants awarded to Martyn Poliakoff by the EPSRC |url=http://gow.epsrc.ac.uk/NGBOViewPerson.aspx?PersonId=12558 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120715130933/http://gow.epsrc.ac.uk/NGBOViewPerson.aspx?PersonId=12558 |archive-date=15 July 2012 |access-date=5 December 2016 |website=Epsrc.ac.uk |publisher=[[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] |location=Swindon}}</ref>

Poliakoff is a global leader in the field of green chemistry with a specific interest in the applications of [[supercritical fluids]]. These highly compressed gases possess properties of gases and liquids that permit interesting chemical reactions without the need for organic solvents, which endanger both health and the environment.<ref name="Anon.-2002" /> His contributions have enabled the development of supercritical carbon dioxide and water solvent systems to replace traditional organic solvents at the industrial scale. As foreign secretary and vice-president of the Royal Society from 2011 to 2016, he worked to represent and further the impact of UK science around the world.<ref name="Anon.-2002" />

===Popular science===
Poliakoff is the narrator in most of a series of over 750 short videos called ''[[Periodic Videos|The Periodic Table of Videos]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Haran |first1=B. |last2=Poliakoff |first2=M. |year=2011 |title=How to measure the impact of chemistry on the small screen |journal=[[Nature Chemistry]] |volume=3 |issue=3 |pages=180–82 |bibcode=2011NatCh...3..180H |doi=10.1038/nchem.990 |issn=1755-4330 |oclc=4795274937 |pmid=21336314}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Haran |first1=B. |author-link1=Brady Haran |last2=Poliakoff |first2=M. |year=2011 |title=The Periodic Table of Videos |journal=Science |volume=332 |issue=6033 |pages=1046–17 |bibcode=2011Sci...332.1046H |doi=10.1126/science.1196980 |issn=0036-8075 |oclc=4898209818 |pmid=21617067 |doi-access=free}}</ref> a [[popular science]] project produced by [[Brady Haran]], originally intended to familiarise the public with all 118 [[Chemical element|elements]] of the [[periodic table]].  The project has since expanded to cover [[molecules]]; there are also several special videos about other chemical topics.{{citation needed|date=April 2022}} He hit the news for calculating that the [[FIFA World Cup Trophy]] could not have been made from solid gold as it would be too heavy to raise aloft.<ref>{{YouTube|GuCgElVlZhk|Chemistry of the World Cup trophy}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=12 June 2010 |title=Professor says World Cup trophy cannot be solid gold |work=[[BBC News]] |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/10301713 |access-date=19 July 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Doubts raised over World Cup trophy |url=http://www.rthk.org.hk/rthk/news/englishnews/20100612/news_20100612_56_675175.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120929070620/http://www.rthk.org.hk/rthk/news/englishnews/20100612/news_20100612_56_675175.htm |archive-date=29 September 2012 |access-date=19 July 2010 |publisher=Rthk.org.hk }}</ref> Poliakoff showed some videos at [[IUPAC]]'s elements inauguration in the Central Club of Scientists of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in Moscow.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Periodic Videos |date=3 March 2017 |title=Elements Inauguration – Periodic Table of Videos |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nkz5ZAL3jSc |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211214/Nkz5ZAL3jSc |archive-date=14 December 2021 |access-date=21 July 2017 |website=YouTube}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Fedorova |first1=Vera |date=3 March 2017 |title=At the inauguration ceremony of the new elements of the Periodic table of D.I. Mendeleev |url=https://www.jinr.ru/posts/at-the-inauguration-ceremony-of-the-new-elements-of-the-periodic-table-of-d-i-mendeleev/ |access-date=21 July 2017 |website=[[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] |language=en-us}}</ref>

In 2019 he collaborated with his daughter Ellen, among others, to produce an experimental version of the periodic table which was turned upside down, to see if that helped young learners get to grips with the underlying mechanisms.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Turning the table |publisher=University of Nottingham |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/vision/vision-turning-table |access-date=11 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Poliakoff |first=Martyn |last2=Makin |first2=Alexis D. J. |last3=Tang |first3=Samantha L. Y. |last4=Poliakoff |first4=Ellen |date=8 April 2019 |title=Turning the periodic table upside down |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41557-019-0253-6 |journal=Nature Chemistry |language=en |volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=391–393 |doi=10.1038/s41557-019-0253-6 |issn=1755-4330|pmid=30962610}}</ref>

===Honours and awards===
Poliakoff was awarded the [[Meldola Medal and Prize]] from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 1976.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Turner |first1=James J. |last2=Poliakoff |first2=Martyn |date=24 July 1997 |title=Obituary : Professor Jeremy Burdett |work=The Independent |location=London |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/obituary--professor-jeremy-burdett-1252237.html |access-date=20 June 2012}}</ref> He was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2002,<ref name="Anon.-2002" /> [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] (FRSC) also in 2002,<ref name="University of Nottingham">{{cite web |title=Martyn Poliakoff |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/chemistry/people/martyn.poliakoff |access-date=17 April 2015 |publisher=University of Nottingham}}</ref> and [[Fellow of the Institution of Chemical Engineers]] (FIChemE) in 2004.<ref name="Professor Sir Martyn Poliakoff">{{cite web |title=Professor Sir Martyn Poliakoff |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/martyn-poliakoff/ |access-date=12 April 2015}}</ref> He served on the IChemE Council between 2009 and 2013.<ref name="Professor Sir Martyn Poliakoff" /> Poliakoff was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2008 New Year Honours]]<ref name="Advisory Council of the Campaign for Science and Engineering">{{cite web |title=Advisory Council of the Campaign for Science and Engineering |url=http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100828110110/http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm |archive-date=28 August 2010 |access-date=11 February 2011}}</ref> and is a member of the Advisory Council for the [[Campaign for Science and Engineering]] since 2008.<ref name="Advisory Council of the Campaign for Science and Engineering" /> In 2008, he was elected an Honorary Member of the Chemical Society of Ethiopia<ref name="Professor Sir Martyn Poliakoff" /> and a Foreign Member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 2011.<ref name="University of Nottingham" /> He took up the positions of Foreign Secretary<ref>{{cite web |last1=Poliakoff |first1=Martyn |title=The Royal Society, the Foreign Secretary, and International Relations |url=http://www.sciencediplomacy.org/letter-field/2015/royal-society-foreign-secretary-and-international-relations |website=Science & Diplomacy |access-date=24 March 2015 |archive-date=16 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190516191053/http://www.sciencediplomacy.org/letter-field/2015/royal-society-foreign-secretary-and-international-relations |url-status=dead }}</ref> and vice-president of the [[Royal Society]] in November 2011, positions which are held for a fixed five-year period.<ref>{{cite web |title=Martyn Poliakoff |url=http://royalsociety.org/people/martyn-poliakoff/ |access-date=5 December 2016 |publisher=[[Royal Society]]}}</ref> In 2011, he won the [[Nyholm Prize for Education]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nyholm Prize for Education 2011 Winner |url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/NyholmPrizeEducation/2011winner.asp |access-date=2 August 2012 |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref>

Poliakoff also received an Honorary Doctorate from [[Heriot-Watt University]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite web |date=23 November 2011 |title=Heriot-Watt University Honorary Graduates |url=http://www.hw.ac.uk/news/archive/2011/heriot-watt-honorary-graduates-november-2011.htm |access-date=5 December 2016 |website=Hw.ac.uk |publisher=Heriot-Watt University |location=Edinburgh}}</ref>

In 2012, Poliakoff was elected a Fellow of the [[Academia Europaea]] and in 2013, an Associate Fellow of [[TWAS]], the World Academy of Science.<ref name="University of Nottingham" /> He was elected an Associate Member of the [[Ethiopian Academy of Sciences]] in 2014.<ref name="Professor Sir Martyn Poliakoff" /> Poliakoff was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2015 New Year Honours]] for services to the chemical sciences.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=61092|date=31 December 2014|page=N2|supp=y}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Order of the Companions of Honour : Members of the Order of the Companions of Honour |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/391413/New_Year_Honours_List_2015.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150102104907/https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/391413/New_Year_Honours_List_2015.pdf |archive-date=2 January 2015 |access-date=5 December 2016 |website=Gov.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=New Year Honours: YouTube sensation Professor Martyn Poliakoff to be knighted for making chemistry fun to learn |url=http://www.nottinghampost.com/New-Year-Honours-YouTube-sensation-Professor/story-25783202-detail/story.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231020824/http://www.nottinghampost.com/New-Year-Honours-YouTube-sensation-Professor/story-25783202-detail/story.html |archive-date=31 December 2014 |access-date=30 December 2014 |publisher=Nottingham Post }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sir Martyn and the Palace – The Periodic Table of Videos |url=http://www.periodicvideos.com/videos/knighthood_palace.htm |access-date=5 December 2016 |website=Periodicvideos.com |publisher=University of Nottingham}}</ref> He was also elected an Honorary Fellow of the [[Chinese Chemical Society (Beijing)|Chinese Chemical Society]] in 2015.<ref name="University of Nottingham" /> Poliakoff was awarded the [[Lord Lewis Prize]] in 2016 for his work concerning the applications of supercritical fluids, and for his work in the development of science policy within the EU and globally.<ref>{{cite web |title=RSC Lord Lewis Prize 2016 Winner |url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/LordLewisPrize/2016-Winner.asp |access-date=14 September 2016 |website=www.rsc.org}}</ref> In 2016, Poliakoff was elected [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (FAAAS),<ref name="University of Nottingham" /> and in 2017 a [[Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering]] (FREng).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 July 2018 |title=Sir Martyn Poliakoff FREng profile |url=https://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/the-fellowship/new-fellows-2017/fellows/martyn-poliakoff |website=Royal Academy of Engineering |access-date=2 July 2018 |archive-date=31 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831003753/https://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/the-fellowship/new-fellows-2017/fellows/martyn-poliakoff |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2019, he was awarded the [[Royal Society of London Michael Faraday Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Recipients of Royal Society medals and awards in 2019 announced &#124; Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2019/07/royal-society-medals-awards-2019/ |website=royalsociety.org}}</ref> for science communication for his work on the ''[[Periodic Videos]]''. He was also awarded the 2019 [[Longstaff Prize]] for his "outstanding contributions to green chemistry and for participating centrally in the creation of the Periodic Table Videos".<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 Longstaff Prize Winner |url=https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/LongstaffPrize/2019-Winner.asp |access-date=10 January 2020 |website=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref> At the end of 2023, Poliakoff was elected (in the division of chemistry) a Foreign Academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>[https://www.chinesechemsoc.org/doi/10.31635/ccschem.023.202301223ed1 Editorial, Jan 2024] - website of the [[Chinese Chemical Society (Beijing)|Chinese Chemical Society]]</ref>

Poliakoff was awarded the American [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS) [[AAAS David and Betty Hamburg Award for Science Diplomacy|David and Betty Hamburg Award for Science Diplomacy]] in 2026.<ref name="UN">{{cite web |title=Chemistry professor honoured with science diplomacy award |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/news/chemistry-professor-honoured-with-science-diplomacy-award |website=University of Nottingham Press Release |publisher=University of Nottingham |access-date=18 May 2026}}</ref>

A tram in [[Nottingham Express Transit|Nottingham's tram network]] was named after him in 2021.<ref>{{cite news |date=16 December 2021 |title=Nottingham tram named in honour of Sir Martyn Poliakoff |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-nottinghamshire-59672285 |access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Poliakoff has a daughter, Ellen Poliakoff, a psychology lecturer at the [[University of Manchester]];<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr Ellen Poliakoff research profile – personal details |url=http://www.manchester.ac.uk/research/ellen.poliakoff/ |publisher=The University of Manchester}}</ref> and a son, Simon Poliakoff, a physics teacher at [[the Priory School, Hitchin]].  Martyn Poliakoff produced a web eulogy of close friend [[Tony Judt]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tony Judt Tribute |url=http://www.periodicvideos.com/videos/feature_tony_judt.htm |access-date=5 December 2016 |website=Periodicvideos.com |publisher=The Periodic Table of Videos}}</ref>
